reason: E1 supports the creation of a heterogeneous ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and mentions microcrack-arresting, but does not involve cryo-rolling or warm rolling. E2 supports the back-stress mechanism from heterogeneous structures in a hybrid-processed EHEA, but the specific cryo-rolling plus warm rolling sequence and its effect on modulus and fracture resistance are not directly evidenced. Thus, some key premises are supported, while others rely on extrapolation or lack direct citation.
premises: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can be processed to an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with hierarchical heterogeneity via tailored thermo-mechanical processing.
Heterogeneous micro/nano-structures generate strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) that produce long-range back stress, enhancing work hardening and ductility.
Hybrid cryo-rolling plus warm rolling and annealing can create a dual heterogeneous nanostructure with refined grains and precipitates at domain boundaries.
The refined heterogeneous structure increases effective Young's modulus and provides crack-shielding via microcrack arrest.
The proposed processing yields a substantial increase in yield strength (10–20% over benchmarks) while maintaining or improving ductility and fracture resistance.
